Treat the two outer components independently.

- For the `image2` identity, use that each partial map `a ↦ l a b` and `b ↦ l a b` is a left adjoint by `h₁` and `h₂`. Left adjoints preserve the nonempty bounded suprema available in a conditionally complete lattice. Reassociate `l ''₂ s t` as an iterated image and establish:
  \[
  \sup_{a\in s,\ b\in t} l(a,b)
  =\sup_{b\in t}l(\sup s,b)
  =l(\sup s,\sup t).
  \]
  The useful intermediate goals are the corresponding one-variable `sSup_image` identities; nonemptiness and boundedness provide exactly the hypotheses needed for conditional suprema.

- For the `Iff`, prove both universally quantified statements directly, so neither implication needs to use its premise. On the `WithTop` side, `s ⊄ {⊤}` supplies an actual finite element of `s`; together with boundedness below, the infimum is therefore finite and is represented by the coercion of the infimum of the finite preimage. On the well-founded-order side, `argminOn id s hs` is a least element of `s`; its membership and minimality make it both a lower bound and an element of the set, hence it equals `sInf s`.

Thus the main mechanisms are preservation of suprema by left adjoints, the finite/`⊤` decomposition of `WithTop`, and characterization of an infimum by an attained minimum.
